output.question: What lawsuits is Costco involved in?
output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, Costco's latest annual filing identifies pending or recently unresolved matters involving employee wage-and-hour claims (including Gray and the still-being-resolved Madera matter), opioid-distribution litigation, website privacy/pixel-tracking claims, Kirkland Signature tequila labeling, tariff pass-throughs, and promotional-email marketing. The filing says the opioid matters still pending include an Ohio third-party-payor claim, infant-injury actions, a Georgia county claim, New York state-court claims, and Pennsylvania district-attorney claims; it also lists pending tariff suits (Stockov, Gower, Ortiz, Briggs) and the Jay email-marketing case. [3](#cite-3) CourtListener's post–August 30 federal-docket search also shows newer Costco cases captioned Cresten Karam, Arce, Moreno II, Betz, Kaci Rebecca Morton, Timothy Alexander Kyle Aragon, and Elaine Rojas, so the SEC list should not be treated as exhaustive through today. [4](#cite-4)

key_facts.fact: Costco's latest 10-K says it is involved in many claims, proceedings, and litigations arising from its business and property ownership.

Employee-related matters include Martin Reyes and Nader wage/PAGA cases; Washington employee class actions Madera and Howell; Howell was dismissed, while Costco reached an agreement to resolve Madera for an immaterial amount subject to court approval.

Gray v. Costco alleges that Costco restricted workers earning less than twice the minimum wage from having a second job in violation of Washington law; the class was certified and trial was set for March 1, 2027.

Costco reports remaining opioid litigation involving an Ohio third-party payor, infant-injury actions, a Georgia county claim, New York state-court claims, and Pennsylvania county-district-attorney claims; Costco says it is defending the pending matters.
Website privacy litigation includes Castillo and related pixel-tracker cases; Birdwell was dismissed with prejudice in March 2026, while the filing describes the Castillo claims as continuing.

Kirkland Signature tequila litigation includes Salisbury; plaintiffs allege products labeled '100% de Agave' contain alcohol derived from non-agave sugars. Glazer was dismissed without prejudice and Costco moved to dismiss Salisbury in April 2026.
Four tariff-refund class actions are Stockov, Gower, Ortiz, and Briggs; the Gower dismissal motion was denied July 17, 2026 and discretionary appellate review was pending.

Zydel concerned promotional-email subject lines and was being administered as a class settlement; a newer Jay case alleges deceptive limited-time email subject lines under Washington, Indiana, and Maryland statutes.

A CourtListener search for exact-party federal dockets filed after August 30, 2026 returned eight Costco-related dockets, including Cresten Karam, Arce, Moreno II, Betz, Kaci Rebecca Morton, Timothy Alexander Kyle Aragon, and Elaine Rojas, plus a Purdue opioid-litigation docket naming Costco.

caveats: The SEC filing is current through August 30, 2026, although it was filed October 7, 2026; matters may have been filed, settled, dismissed, or changed after that cutoff.

Costco states that it does not believe any pending matter, individually or in aggregate, will have a material adverse effect, but an unfavorable outcome could still be material to an individual quarter or year.

The CourtListener search is limited to federal RECAP/PACER dockets and its keyless results do not provide complete allegations or status for every case; it is not a complete nationwide lawsuit inventory.
Several matters in the 10-K are described as resolved, dismissed, stayed, or subject to settlement approval rather than fully active lawsuits.
